correctness.rationale: The nine-point order is explicitly fixed by cover relations. Exhaustive generation gives 12,575 isotone self-maps; each is rechecked against the full transitive closure. Exact pointwise-comparability components have sizes 12,573, 1, and 1; the isolated maps are exactly the two automorphisms, and all nine constants lie in the large component. Stong's finite-space homotopy criterion then proves the three homotopy classes. The opposite-space statement follows because reversing both orders preserves the set of isotone functions and reverses only the pointwise mapping order.

value.rationale: The poset is the minimum-cardinality weakly contractible but noncontractible finite space, so its ordinary self-homotopy monoid is a canonical invariant of the failure of a Whitehead-type implication in finite spaces. The complete classification is structural: exactly two isolated non-null automorphism classes survive, while every non-homeomorphism is null. This is a natural whole-object classification rather than an arbitrary finite slice, and it yields a reproducible benchmark for finite mapping-space algorithms.
